title: Shared compute-host failure disrupts multiple critical services
alert_or_symptom: The customer web portal, user authentication and payment processing became unavailable simultaneously after most Application Compute Cluster worker nodes failed.

technical_evidence.observation: Eight of ten worker nodes changed to NotReady between 14:02 and 14:03. The cluster reports insufficient remaining capacity to schedule the affected application workloads.

The underlying hosts supporting the eight failed worker nodes report host-unavailable and virtual-machine-termination events. The events occurred before the affected application replicas became unavailable.
Customer Web Portal, Identity and Access Service and Payment Processing Service replicas are unavailable because their workloads cannot run on the remaining compute capacity.
Portal transaction success fell to 0 percent, token issuance success fell to 0.5 percent and payment-processing success fell to 0.9 percent after the compute-host failures.
The DNS, CDN and Load-Balancing Platform, Transaction Database Cluster, Message Broker and Object Storage Platform remain healthy and reachable.
Customers across the United Kingdom and Ireland cannot load the portal, sign in or complete payment. No approved alternative customer channel is available.

The shared Application Compute Cluster host failure directly explains the simultaneous loss of the affected workloads. The precise physical or hypervisor-level mechanism responsible for the host failures has not yet been determined.

service_impact.user_impact_description: Customers across the United Kingdom and Ireland cannot access the web portal, authenticate or complete payment because multiple critical application workloads cannot run on the remaining compute capacity.
service_impact.business_function_affected: Customer digital access, authentication and payment processing

environmental_context: The Application Compute Cluster is a Tier 1 shared infrastructure platform.
The Customer Web Portal, Identity and Access Service and Payment Processing Service are Tier 1 critical services hosted on the cluster.
The affected workloads require cluster compute capacity to run.
The edge, database, messaging and storage platforms remain healthy.
reported_unknowns: The precise physical, virtualisation or hypervisor-level mechanism that caused the compute hosts to become unavailable.
Whether the failed hosts can safely return to service or replacement capacity will be required.
The expected restoration time for sufficient compute capacity and the affected services.
Whether any in-flight authentication or payment requests require subsequent integrity verification.
additional_context: No data loss, corruption, duplicate payment or serious security exposure has been confirmed.
The incident affects multiple independently owned critical application services through one directly evidenced shared compute-platform failure.
